sections.h2: What does the Yadkin County Register of Deeds handle?
sections.html:
This office in Yadkinville keeps the county's land records: deeds, deeds of trust, maps and related filings. State law opens those records to public inspection. The staff also copy and certify birth, death and marriage certificates, issue marriage licenses and swear in notaries.

A sale is only fully protected once the deed is on the books. Under G.S. 47-18, an unregistered conveyance loses to lien creditors and later buyers who paid value, and whoever registers first generally ranks first.

The county web page urges electronic recording for every document. Marriage licenses and notary oaths run by appointment through 336-849-7904. Yadkin County voters choose the register of deeds, and that same office takes the deed excise tax at the time of recording.

sections.h2: How does a deed get on record after a Yadkin County sale?
sections.html:
Usually the attorney or title company at the closing table sends it electronically. The register accepts every document type except maps by e-recording. Any firm wanting to submit must go through Simplifile, CSC or ePN and complete a submitter agreement that the provider passes to the county.

The Yadkin County tax office page has a one-line instruction for deed work: consult your attorney, then it links to the Register of Deeds. Sellers in Yadkinville, Jonesville, East Bend or on a rural road in between therefore rarely deal with the recording desk themselves.

  • Ask whether your closing firm already has an e-recording agreement with Yadkin County.
  • Find out who is writing the check for the excise tax, since the statute assigns it to the seller.
  • Keep the recording confirmation as proof of the date and time of registration.
  • Bringing paper instead? Phone the office before you drive, because no walk-in recording hours appear on the county page.

sections.h2: What does recording cost at the Yadkin County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
A single statewide schedule applies here. G.S. 161-10 prints one schedule for the whole state, calls it complete and exclusive, and requires payment up front.

Register of Deeds charges in G.S. 161-10 that touch a house sale
DocumentAmount printed
Deed, pages 1 through 15$26.00
Mortgage, pages 1 through 35$64.00
Overflow pages on either$4.00 each
Paying off a mortgage (satisfaction)Free
Certified copy of a recorded deed$5.00 plus $2.00 per added page
Nonstandard document$25.00 added

Count the pages in your deed and exhibits before closing, because the $4.00 charge starts on the sixteenth page of a general instrument.

sections.h2: Who owes the excise stamp on a Yadkin County deed?
sections.html:
The person transferring the house. G.S. 105-228.30 puts the rate at one dollar per five hundred dollars of value. Payment is due at the register's counter ahead of the filing.

Collections are divided evenly. Yadkin County keeps its half, and the other half moves to the Department of Revenue every month after refunds and an allowance, with the county entitled to hold back 2 percent of the state share. The closing statement lists the dollar figure that applies to your price.

If a house passes as a gift or between relatives, ask the office how a stated value is treated before anyone signs.

sections.h2: Where does the tax office fit in with the Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
They are separate counters. The Yadkin County Tax Department in Yadkinville lists and bills property, takes exemption applications and keeps the parcel maps. The register of deeds only records the paper. The tax office page announces a 2027 revaluation and points deed questions back to an attorney and the Register of Deeds.

For billing and payment questions, the tax office takes calls at 336-849-7903. It lists an August discount of 2 percent, plus a solid waste fee of $76.00 per household, or $38.00 with the elderly exemption. Statewide, taxes fall due September 1, and interest starts January 6 (G.S. 105-360).

sections.h2: Which other documents are recorded at the Yadkin County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
More than deeds. Under G.S. 47-18, options, leases longer than three years and rights of first refusal also need registration to bind later buyers and lien creditors. A seller who gave a buyer an option months ago should check that it was recorded, since an unrecorded one may not hold up against a new purchaser.

A seller-financed sale is the other case worth knowing. North Carolina's Chapter 47H covers a contract for deed with five or more payments, where the seller keeps title. Written and acknowledged terms are required, the buyer gets a three-business-day cancellation window, and the seller records the contract or a memorandum within five business days. A forfeiture notice has to allow at least 30 days to cure (Chapter 47H).

  • Satisfactions of a deed of trust record for no fee under G.S. 161-10, so paying off a mortgage costs nothing at this office.
  • For a parcel split between counties, the excise tax goes to the county holding the greater value.
  • An estate sale may require a small estate affidavit to list each tract the decedent owned.

sections.h2: What does the Yadkin County housing picture look like?
sections.html:
Yadkin County counted 38,325 people in mid-2025, up 3.0 percent from the 2020 estimates base and still a little under its 2010 census figure of 38,406. About 111 people live on each of its 334.94 land square miles, and there are 17,697 housing units.

Owners live in 76.9 percent of Yadkin County homes. The five-year survey for 2020 to 2024 gives $181,200 as the middle home value, $1,177 a month in costs for owners with a mortgage and $766 in rent. Households earn a median $62,932, and 14.5 percent of people fall below the poverty line. Adults 65 and over are 22.4 percent of residents and 1,966 are veterans, so the age-based and veteran programs reach many owners.

The county had 650 employer establishments and 8,235 jobs in 2023, and workers travel 29.6 minutes on average to reach work. New construction is slow, with 116 building permits in 2025. Resales of inherited and older houses make up much of the activity, and for an estate sale the clerk of superior court can tell you who has authority to sign.

sections.h2: How do Yadkin County's economy and demographics shape a home sale?
sections.html:
Retail sales were $338,224 thousand in 2022, or $9,018 per resident, according to the Census Bureau, a lower per-person figure than a county with a large shopping district would show. Health care and social assistance brought in receipts of $66,701 thousand and transportation and warehousing $57,494 thousand. The county had 2,727 nonemployer businesses in 2024, which fits a place with many self-employed households.

Among adults 25 and older, 86.6 percent finished high school and 17.5 percent hold a bachelor's degree. About 87.9 percent of households have a broadband subscription, which matters to buyers who work remotely, and 11.7 percent of residents under 65 lack health insurance. Roughly 20.7 percent of residents are under 18.

For a seller, the practical point is a buyer pool drawn from nearby employers and commuters. Anyone selling out of an inherited house or a tax lien situation should know that the county posts tax foreclosure sales on its website under Tax Foreclosure Sales, and that an owner can still redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes, penalties, interest and costs.

faqs.q: Does Yadkin County charge a transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: North Carolina charges an excise tax, and the seller pays it at the register of deeds before the deed is filed. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars of value.

faqs.q: Can a Yadkin County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes, any document except a map. The attorney or title company must first sign a submitter agreement through Simplifile, CSC or ePN. For paper filings, phone 336-849-7904.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record a satisfaction of a mortgage in Yadkin County?
faqs.a: No. G.S. 161-10 lists no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust, so recording a payoff costs nothing at the Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: How long does a buyer under a Yadkin County contract for deed have to cancel?
faqs.a: Until midnight of the third business day after the contract is signed or delivered. The seller then has five business days to record the contract or a memorandum of it.

faqs.q: Is a Yadkin County revaluation coming?
faqs.a: Yes, the county tax page says a 2027 revaluation is underway. Counties must reappraise all real estate on an eight-year cycle at the longest.
